.qc-cache/hireops-live-desk-2026-10-02-r1/task/tests/{scored,gates}/*/judge.toml (mode, aggregation and criterion counts; pattern search of criterion text, not a full read of all 152 functional criteria)
evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode = "batched" with aggregation = "weighted_mean" (functional 152 criteria, polish 5, visual 5); both gates use aggregation = "all_pass" and are exempt. Each scored prompt carries explicit independence plus continue-after-failure wording. functional/prompt.md:15: "Once this basic gate succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failure, and preserve successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared scenarios reduce repeated setup; they are not conjunctive scoring bundles." Reinforced at :9 ("give that criterion its lowest score ... state what you observed, and move on"), :23 ("a failed cell must not erase successful sibling cells"), :45 ("One failed claim must not erase unrelated financial or permission observations"), :55 ("do not make later concurrency credit inherit the earlier pair's failure"), :61/:63/:73 ("The failed branch's own criterion stays 0" while a simpler setup is used for other rows). polish/prompt.md:12: "Otherwise judge each criterion independently, continue after failures and preserve valid observations. A failed recovery branch must not erase other observed recovery credit." and :14 "Continue independent checks after any sibling failure." visual/prompt.md:12: "Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures." A pattern search of the three scored prompts, the three scored judge.toml files and app_context.md for stop-at-first-failure wording (stop at/on/after, first failure, skip remaining, do not continue, fail all, cross-criterion 'if hro_x fails') found no such instruction. The only all-or-nothing rule in each scored prompt is the global browser gate (functional:15 "gives every binary criterion0", polish:12 "binary0 throughout", visual:12 "every criterion its minimum raw Likert score1"); this mirrors the frozen template, whose scored prompts say "If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension" and whose polish prompt states "The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension", so it is not a one-criterion-zeroes-the-rest defect. Counterexample attempts: (a) a broken app failing one mid-protocol step (e.g. P4 revision) cannot zero later rows by prompt instruction, because the prompt directs dedicated simpler controls and keeps only the owning row at 0; (b) a conforming app is not zeroed by a sibling's failure. Limits of this review: it is a static wording check. The private check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed, and no configured judge run exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'), so whether the configured judge actually obeys the wording across 152 batched criteria within its budget is unmeasured; that belongs to the workload/runtime rows and is not waived here. The 152 functional criterion texts were pattern-searched, not individually read, for cross-criterion dependencies; row 28 owns that question.
